about: Does this site's use of IPMA's warnings meet MeteoAlarm's Terms and Conditions (https://www.meteoalarm.org/en/live/page/terms-and-conditions, last updated 15/03/2024, read 2026-11-10T23:53Z)? Checked by incident.weatherwatch@web-summit.dinis at the conductor's request. The terms apply to what we take from MeteoAlarm's feed (data/weather/cap.json and what is written from it); warnings.json comes from api.ipma.pt and falls under IPMA's own terms. A careful reading, not legal advice.
what_we_take_from_meteoalarm: incidents/2026-11-10-storm-charles/data/weather/cap.json (17 CAP messages for the Lisbon district, read by data/weather/tools/refresh.py from https://feeds.meteoalarm.org/api/v1/warnings/feeds-portugal), served at its path and under api/v1/; the sent times in timeline.md and on the home page come from it.

requirements.term: the relevant national service named (single country)
requirements.where: cap.json says "IPMA's warnings"; the pages name IPMA throughout
cap.json: sent_utc on every message; the timeline quotes it ("IPMA sent the change at 21:23")

requirements.term: a link to www.meteoalarm.org in internet applications
requirements.where: cap.json's source is the feed address (feeds.meteoalarm.org), not www.meteoalarm.org; the served home page and incident page contain no mention of MeteoAlarm at all (0 matches in their HTML at 23:58Z), although the home page shows times taken from its feed. datasets.html mentions it once.
requirements.fix: add "via MeteoAlarm (EUMETNET)" with a link to https://www.meteoalarm.org wherever a CAP sent time is shown, and a meteoalarm field in cap.json

requirements.where: not on any page or in cap.json
requirements.fix: publish, on the pages that show CAP-derived content and in cap.json: "Time delays between this website and the www.meteoalarm.org website are possible. For the most up-to-date awareness information as published by the participating National Meteorological and Hydrological Services, please refer to www.meteoalarm.org."

requirements.term: if operationally redistributed: real time, delay on average under five minutes and never over ten
requirements.where: cap.json is refreshed by an agent's run and a commit, about every 30 minutes (read 23:53:38Z, next_read_utc 00:22Z). The message IPMA sent at 21:23Z entered cap.json at the 23:51Z read: about two and a half hours later.
requirements.fix: either (a) present cap.json as a dated record, not a live service (it already carries read_utc; say so in words next to it and keep the disclaimer), which is the reading under which the rule for "operational" redistribution does not bind; or (b) refresh it every five minutes by a scheduled job. The browser cannot read the feed itself: the feed sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header (checked 23:58Z).

requirements.term: if modified, redistributed along with the same Information without material change
requirements.where: cap.json keeps IPMA's own event and description text in Portuguese, unedited, for one district; it is a selection, not a rewording. English summaries on the pages sit beside links to the source.

requirements.term: MeteoAlarm's own Content (maps, icons, design) not copied

lacking: the ten-minute delay (or words saying cap.json is a dated record, not a live feed)
owners: cap.json and refresh.py: incident.meteorologist@; the pages: incident.conductor@ and incident.designer@. This agent changed none of them.
ipma_terms_for_warnings_json: IPMA asks that the source always be named (met: "IPMA" and a link to api.ipma.pt on every item) and that its logo be used, with a link to its site, when its information is included in web pages: the logo is not on our pages. Whether to add it is the designer's and Dinis's call.
